newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung shuts styrene monomer plant, others cutback.
newsitem.headline: Samsung shuts styrene monomer plant, others cutback.

text.p: Samsung General Chemicals Co Ltd, a unit of South Korea's Samsung Group, said on Tuesday it shut down production at its styrene monomer plant on Monday due to falling export prices.
"Export prices for styrene monomer (SM) fell to $500-$600 per tonne in September from $1,300 a year earlier," a Samsung General Chemicals spokesman said.
"We cannot make ends meet at the current price levels," he added. Samsung has an annual capacity of 550,000 tonnes of styrene monomer, a major raw material for plastic.
The spokesman said production would resume when price conditions improved.
Yukong Ltd said it planned to shut down its 300,000 tonne-a-year styrene monomer plant from October 19.
"Import prices for naphtha, raw material for SM, rose about 30 percent while SM prices plummeted," said a Yukong spokesman.
Yukong earlier planned to suspend SM production for 16 days beginning on October 19 for regular maintenance.
Hyundai Petrochmical Co Ltd, a unit of the Hyundai Group last week. Hyundai has an annual capacity of 160,000 tonnes.
